rubric_notes: Fully verified: release 2.08 and periodic label from /releases/current, lineage sunids, all five families with children listings, fold a.22 shown to have a single superfamily, homology endpoint for a.22 noting no homology above superfamily, and H1 lineage (a.4.5.13 under a.4.5 winged helix). Reasoning cleanly separates superfamily-level probable common ancestry from family-level closeness, refuses transfer of DNA-packaging function, partner pairing or template use, and notes absence of warnings is not extra evidence. States unverified items explicitly. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct release context (2.08 stable, periodic update noted), sccs, sunids, names, species. Interprets superfamily as probable common ancestry, not family-level; lists function-transfer limits for both HisE and MazG labels, templates, ligands, boundaries (7-93), evolutionary history; notes curator rationale not exposed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct and bundle-supported classification: c.55.1 (53067), c.55.1.1 (53068), c.55.1.3 (53083), c.55.1.4 (53089), lineage, release 2.08 as current stable, d3atua1/d3atua2 as c.55.1.1 HSP70 domains. Superfamily correctly treated as homology level, fold as structural only; rejects transfer of substrate, reaction, mechanism and template use. Omits the gold-named limits on regulation and oligomeric state. Claim that homology/annotation endpoints returned 404 for the c.55.1 node is unverifiable from the bundle but is not used to support any biological claim. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Most thoroughly evidenced answer: family and superfamily homology/annotation records, Pfam PF05067 mapping, superfamily comment, fold siblings all supported. Correct divergent-homology reading, explicit rejection of function/metal/mechanism/oligomer transfer, and a correct note that different superfamilies would not imply convergence. Omits the positive statement of what evidence (family-specific sequence, structural, experimental data) is required to assign chemistry or role; only says it did not inspect alignments or literature. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct 2.08 lineages for b.6.1.1 (49504), b.6.1.5 (74874), b.6.1.6 (110107) under b.6.1 Cupredoxins (49503), all supported by the parents/search bundle. Interprets superfamily as a homology-bearing level implying probable common ancestry, distinguishes family vs superfamily, rejects copper/electron-transfer transfer and names required evidence (conserved ligand residues, metal records, experimental redox data). Flags general-knowledge statements and retrieval limits. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy with sunids, UBX lineage, Pfam PF00789 and family homology flag all supported; current-release facts supported. Probable common ancestry at superfamily, family as closer level; rejects conjugation, p97 and Ras transfers, name-based assignment (bundle-supported a.4.1.1 and c.47.1.24 hits), fold-only ancestry, and non-homology over-reading; limits clearly stated.

All classifications and sunids correct and supported (52172, 52171, 51349, 52173 with d1u0sy_ T. maritima, 52252, 82344 with d1r8ja2 2-135, sibling families); superfamily-level homology (scope sf, no warnings) and empty annotation comments correctly reported, with the sensible caveat that absence of warnings is not positive evidence. Reasoning: shared superfamily means probable common ancestry, not family-level closeness; rejects phosphorylation/Asp/phosphotransfer transfer, decarboxylation/PLP transfer, clock/KaiB/KaiC transfer, and template/substrate/mechanism inference from placement; notes KaiA function sits in its a.186.1.1 domain and wing catalysis belongs to the enzyme's other domain; distinguishes fold/class similarity. No material issues. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

All identifiers, example domains across species, 'complexed with adp' comment, homology flags and PubMed are supported by bundle. Two-level interpretation is correct: homology claimed among V1/A1 bulge domains at superfamily/family level, fold shared with b.84.1-b.84.4 without any positive homology assertion, and separate superfamilies do not prove analogy or convergence. Rejects function/template transfer and notes curator rationale unverified. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Release 2.08, class f (56835), fold f.21 (81344) with comment, three superfamily sunids, and the three superfamily homology records (scope sf, no warnings/heterogeneity/repeats) all supported by the bundle. Correct fold-vs-superfamily reading, explicit that separate superfamilies are not proof of analogy or independent origin, external sequence/structure/literature evidence required for either direction, and function/substrate/template transfer rejected. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All must_include met: c.2.1.1/c.2.1.8/c.2.1.9 under c.2.1 with correct sunids, superfamily read as probable remote common ancestry, explicit statement that ligand, catalysis, channel regulation and whole-protein role need family-specific evidence. Explicitly rejects inferring NAD(P)H binding for CoA domain or dehydrogenase activity for RCK domain. Homology scope 'sf', no warnings, and single-superfamily fold c.2 all supported by bundle. AcdA example supported by c.2.1.8 parents. Clearly separates verified SCOPe facts from background knowledge. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Meets all must_include items: same family k.40.1.1 (sunid 100905), the family node comment 'not a true family' retrieved from the family annotations endpoint, and the calibrated conclusion that the shared placement is a designed structural grouping with no meaningful positive homology claim. Correctly explains that homology_implied_by_level=true is generic and does not override the comment, notes the annotation does not prove the pair unrelated, refuses function/template transfer, and states limits. All identifiers and lineage match the bundle.

Both releases queried and correct: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 own fold/superfamily vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 and d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 sharing superfamily 52309. Explicitly separates sunid persistence/sid change from the re-parenting, framing the change as a new superfamily-level homology assertion rather than a rename. Correct caveats on function transfer, unknown intermediate release, and unverified rationale.

Correct d1a14h2 lineage with sunids, l.1.1.1, N-terminal tag residues 1-8, annotation comment, and homology warning all supported. d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 class b stated with explicit limit that its lineage was not checked (must_include satisfied). Clear statement that tag matches reflect shared constructs not ancestry and that class l family/superfamily/fold labels carry no evolutionary meaning. States limits. No errors.

Complete: queried each release and confirms single domain through 2.03 and the 2.04 to 2.08 split with correct boundaries and lineages. Strong module interpretation, good limits (shows the change not the rationale), and sound per-domain homology-search guidance.

All classifications, boundaries and sunids correct and bundle-supported; mosaic interpretation, new fold d.394, and strong limits (no nonhomology inference, no function transfer, novelty is release-relative). Overgeneralizes that 'the family-level placements are new Prp8-specific families' for all four reused domains; d3jb9a4 is in the shared Bromodomain family a.29.2.1. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Complete: lineage with sunids, 're' flag on two domains, 'single repeat', canonical repeat unit and coordinate scope, no homology warnings. Correct repeat-based interpretation and appropriate caveats on specificity and template use.

Correct metadata and periodic label (bundle-supported). Cites stable 2.08 as reproducible identifier with release-scoped paths; periodic label as supplementary note only; states periodic is not a new stable release and is a weaker reproducibility basis. Omits that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable domains. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Thorough and supported: correct a.47.2.1 placement, sunids, lineage, automated-matches node, fragment comment, 'ms' flag and homology output, with explicit scoping of what was retrieved. Interpretation correctly reads the spectrin-repeat comment as showing why fragment-only fold calls are unreliable, makes the full domain the basis for fold description, separates fold from superfamily homology, and rejects function/template use of fragments. One noncentral slip: 1dn1 chain A's sccs is written 'e.1.25.1.1' instead of e.25.1.1.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Covers all must_include: convergence as a hypothesis in unrelated folds, divergence supported at family/superfamily, and homology inferred from topology, core alignment, sequence correspondence, motifs in context, architecture and phylogeny. Correctly states SCOPe makes no positive claim between superfamilies and that different placement is not proof of analogy. No must_avoid violations. Factual: no identifiers (explicitly flagged); the statement that the Rossmann NAD(P)-binding fold 'has many superfamilies' is imprecise (c.2 holds a single superfamily c.2.1), a noncentral slip.

Correct before/after classifications with b.23.2 vs b.18.1 in 2.04 and b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3 in 2.08; family 267607 correct. Explicitly remote superfamily-level ancestry, not family-level, structure-discovered with low sequence. Notes absence of warnings is not positive evidence and rejects function/template transfer. Meets all must_include, no must_avoid breach.

All lineage, sunids, boundaries (1ztr A:0-59), comments, and the domain-scope non-inherited hf definition match the evidence bundle. Homology retained via family placement; hf correctly read as a different fold despite similar sequence/SS count; clear limits on fold-level structural equivalence, template use, function transfer, and dataset handling (stratify/exclude, preserve flag, redundancy handling). States what cannot be inferred (actual conformation, curator rationale, no SPACI ranking). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Complete. Verified lineage, protein nodes, fr annotation (domain-level, non-inherited, also in heterogeneity), comment, and quality records for both entries (1uc6 NMR AEROSPACI 0.0216; 1o5d X-ray 2.05 Å AEROSPACI 0.2875) all match bundle. Correctly states quality does not override fragment flag and is not a homology score. Homology retained; alignment coverage caveats; complete unflagged domain as representative; fragment kept labeled when sole structure; diversity stratified by fr. Release semantics (2.08 stable vs periodic update) supported. Limits clearly stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation; family placement asserts homology and a stronger lineage claim; new superfamily is a statement about missing evidence, not analogy/convergence/proven nonhomology, revisable by merge; new fold requires genuinely different arrangement/topology and would hide real similarity otherwise; three-step decision logic integrating alignment, core-position sequence, motifs, architecture and phylogenetic evidence; checks boundaries/annotations; no function/template transfer. No fabricated identifiers. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct 2.08 lineage and sunids for d.144.1, d.144, class d and the three families; superfamily annotation comment and homology record are supported by the bundle. Reasoning is complete: superfamily implies probable common ancestry and a shared two-lobed ATP-binding architecture; substrate class, templates, regulation and motif conservation explicitly not inferable; evidence list covers same-family homology, active-site alignment, biochemistry, full-length regulatory architecture and artifact checks. Minor factual-support issue: the APH protein-node sunids (103302, 64412) are attributed to a search whose response is absent from the evidence bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
